ragnarok.title: No Formal Information Security Management System (ISMS) Governance
ragnarok.description: The organization has not established a documented, approved, and operating information security management framework with defined scope, objectives, responsibilities, risk processes, and continual-improvement mechanisms.
ragnarok.summary: No Formal Information Security Management System (ISMS) Governance: The organization has not established a documented, approved, and operating information security management framework with defined scope, objectives, responsibilities, risk processes, and continual-improvement mechanisms.
ragnarok.impact: Security activities may be inconsistent, risk decisions may be undocumented, and management may be unable to demonstrate that information security is governed systematically.
ragnarok.recommendation: Establish and operate an ISMS governance model approved by executive management.

evidence.summary: No approved ISMS charter, defined ISMS scope, security governance cadence, or consolidated control ownership matrix was available for review.

remediation.solution: Establish and operate an ISMS governance model approved by executive management.
steps: Define organizational context, interested parties, and ISMS scope
Appoint an executive sponsor and accountable security owner
Approve an information security policy and supporting standards
Define measurable security objectives and reporting cadence
Establish risk assessment and risk treatment methodology
Create a control ownership / RACI matrix
Schedule management reviews and internal audits
Track corrective actions and continual improvement
remediation.validation: Approved ISMS scope, policy set, governance minutes, control ownership matrix, risk register, internal audit plan, and evidence of at least one management review cycle.
remediation.priorityRationale: Foundational governance gap affecting the design and operation of most downstream controls.
references: AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria (revised points of focus 2022)

ragnarok.title: Enterprise Information Security Risk Assessment Not Performed
ragnarok.description: A documented information security risk assessment covering systems, data, threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact, existing controls, and residual risk has not been completed or maintained.
ragnarok.summary: Enterprise Information Security Risk Assessment Not Performed: A documented information security risk assessment covering systems, data, threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact, existing controls, and residual risk has not been completed or maintained.
ragnarok.impact: Material risks may remain unidentified or untreated, and control investments may not be risk-based.
ragnarok.recommendation: Implement a repeatable enterprise information security risk assessment and treatment process.

evidence.summary: No current risk register, documented scoring methodology, risk treatment plan, or evidence of periodic reassessment was provided.

remediation.solution: Implement a repeatable enterprise information security risk assessment and treatment process.
steps: Define risk criteria, scoring scales, and risk appetite / acceptance authority
Inventory critical assets, services, data, dependencies, and threat scenarios
Assess inherent likelihood and impact
Document existing controls and control effectiveness
Calculate residual risk
Select treatment: mitigate, transfer, avoid, or accept
Assign owners and target dates
Review risks at least annually and after significant changes
remediation.validation: Current approved risk methodology, populated risk register, treatment plans, risk acceptance records, and evidence of periodic review.
remediation.priorityRationale: Risk assessment is the basis for selecting and justifying controls under ISO 27001 and for SOC 2 risk-based control design.
references: AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria (revised points of focus 2022)

ragnarok.title: Privileged Access Is Not Centrally Controlled
ragnarok.description: Administrative and other highly privileged access is not consistently governed through centralized identity controls, least privilege, strong authentication, approval, and periodic review.
ragnarok.summary: Privileged Access Is Not Centrally Controlled: Administrative and other highly privileged access is not consistently governed through centralized identity controls, least privilege, strong authentication, approval, and periodic review.
ragnarok.impact: Compromise or misuse of privileged credentials could result in broad unauthorized access, system changes, data exposure, or service disruption.
ragnarok.recommendation: Implement privileged access management and enforce least privilege for all administrative access.

evidence.summary: Evidence of centralized privileged-role approval, MFA enforcement for all administrators, privileged account inventory, and recurring access recertification was not available.

remediation.solution: Implement privileged access management and enforce least privilege for all administrative access.
steps: Inventory privileged accounts and roles across cloud, SaaS, infrastructure, databases, and applications
Eliminate shared administrator accounts
Require MFA and phishing-resistant methods where supported
Use separate admin and standard-user identities
Implement just-in-time / time-bound privileged elevation
Require documented approval for privileged grants
Log privileged activity and alert on anomalous use
Recertify privileged access at least quarterly
Immediately revoke privileged access on termination or role change
remediation.validation: Privileged account inventory, MFA policy evidence, approval records, JIT/PAM configuration, quarterly review records, and sample logs showing privileged activity is captured.
remediation.priorityRationale: Privileged access creates a direct path to high-impact compromise and should be addressed before lower-risk access hygiene issues.
references: AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria (revised points of focus 2022)

ragnarok.title: Security Logging and Monitoring Is Insufficient for Critical Systems
ragnarok.description: Critical systems are not consistently configured to generate, centralize, retain, correlate, and review security-relevant logs.
ragnarok.summary: Security Logging and Monitoring Is Insufficient for Critical Systems: Critical systems are not consistently configured to generate, centralize, retain, correlate, and review security-relevant logs.
ragnarok.impact: Security incidents may go undetected or be detected too late; forensic investigation and evidence preservation may be incomplete.
ragnarok.recommendation: Establish centralized security logging, detection, alerting, and review for in-scope systems.

iso27001.name: Assessment and decision on information security events

evidence.summary: No complete logging standard, centralized log-source inventory, retention schedule, alert coverage matrix, or evidence of recurring security-event review was available.

remediation.solution: Establish centralized security logging, detection, alerting, and review for in-scope systems.
steps: Define minimum log events for identity, administrative actions, applications, databases, endpoints, network, and cloud control planes
Synchronize system clocks
Forward logs to a protected centralized platform / SIEM
Define retention by security, legal, and contractual requirements
Create priority detections for authentication abuse, privilege changes, malware, exfiltration, and configuration changes
Assign alert ownership and response SLAs
Test detections using simulated events
Review detection coverage at least quarterly
remediation.validation: Logging standard, log-source inventory, SIEM configuration, retention settings, alert rules, incident tickets generated from test events, and quarterly coverage review.
remediation.priorityRationale: Lack of monitoring can make other preventive controls unverifiable and materially weaken incident detection capability.
references: AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria (revised points of focus 2022)

ragnarok.title: Incident Response Program Is Not Operationalized or Tested
ragnarok.description: The organization lacks a sufficiently documented and tested process for preparation, detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery, evidence handling, communications, and lessons learned.
ragnarok.summary: Incident Response Program Is Not Operationalized or Tested: The organization lacks a sufficiently documented and tested process for preparation, detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery, evidence handling, communications, and lessons learned.
ragnarok.impact: A real incident could result in delayed containment, inconsistent decisions, loss of evidence, regulatory or contractual notification failures, and extended downtime.
ragnarok.recommendation: Create, approve, exercise, and continuously improve a formal incident response program.

iso27001.name: Information security incident management planning and preparation
Assessment and decision on information security events

soc2.name: Identifies, develops, and implements recovery activities

evidence.summary: No approved incident response plan, severity model, contact tree, breach decision workflow, tabletop results, or after-action records were available.

remediation.solution: Create, approve, exercise, and continuously improve a formal incident response program.
steps: Document roles, severity levels, escalation paths, and decision authority
Create playbooks for common scenarios such as ransomware, credential compromise, data exposure, SaaS compromise, and third-party incidents
Define legal, privacy, insurance, customer, and regulator notification decision points
Establish evidence preservation and chain-of-custody procedures
Maintain internal and external contact lists
Run at least annual tabletop exercises and targeted technical simulations
Document lessons learned and corrective actions
Track response metrics such as MTTD and MTTR
remediation.validation: Approved IR plan and playbooks, exercise attendance and scenario records, lessons-learned report, corrective-action tracker, and evidence that contact/escalation information is current.
remediation.priorityRationale: An untested response process materially increases impact when preventive controls fail.

ragnarok.title: MFA Is Not Enforced for All In-Scope Remote and Sensitive Access
ragnarok.description: Multi-factor authentication is not consistently enforced for remote access, administrative access, cloud consoles, and sensitive business applications.
ragnarok.summary: MFA Is Not Enforced for All In-Scope Remote and Sensitive Access: Multi-factor authentication is not consistently enforced for remote access, administrative access, cloud consoles, and sensitive business applications.
ragnarok.impact: Stolen or reused passwords may be sufficient to obtain unauthorized access to sensitive systems or data.
ragnarok.recommendation: Require MFA for all remote, privileged, and sensitive application access, minimizing legacy authentication exceptions.

evidence.summary: MFA coverage evidence for all in-scope systems and user populations was incomplete, and no documented exception process was available.

remediation.solution: Require MFA for all remote, privileged, and sensitive application access, minimizing legacy authentication exceptions.
steps: Inventory authentication paths
Prioritize administrators, remote access, email, cloud consoles, source control, finance, and production systems
Enable MFA centrally through the identity provider where possible
Disable legacy/basic authentication
Use phishing-resistant factors for privileged users where supported
Document time-bound exceptions with compensating controls
Monitor MFA bypass and enrollment events
remediation.validation: Identity-provider policy export, application coverage matrix, screenshots/configuration proving enforcement, exception register, and sampled authentication logs.
remediation.priorityRationale: Credential theft is common; MFA provides high-value risk reduction and supports both frameworks' logical access expectations.
references: AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria (revised points of focus 2022)

ragnarok.title: User Access Reviews Are Not Performed Periodically
ragnarok.description: User and service-account access to systems and sensitive data is not periodically recertified by accountable system or data owners.
ragnarok.summary: User Access Reviews Are Not Performed Periodically: User and service-account access to systems and sensitive data is not periodically recertified by accountable system or data owners.
ragnarok.impact: Excessive, stale, or inappropriate access may persist unnoticed, increasing the likelihood and impact of misuse or compromise.
ragnarok.recommendation: Establish risk-based access recertification for all in-scope systems.

evidence.summary: No complete recurring access review schedule, reviewer sign-off records, or remediation evidence for identified access exceptions was available.

remediation.solution: Establish risk-based access recertification for all in-scope systems.
steps: Define review frequency by sensitivity; use at least quarterly for privileged access and at least semiannual for critical applications
Generate authoritative user/role entitlement reports
Require managers, system owners, or data owners to attest access
Explicitly identify inactive, duplicate, shared, and excessive accounts
Track removals and modifications to closure
Retain reviewer evidence and timestamps
Measure overdue reviews and unresolved exceptions
remediation.validation: Completed access review packages, reviewer approvals, exception tickets, and evidence that rejected access was removed promptly.
remediation.priorityRationale: Access can accumulate over time; recurring recertification is necessary to demonstrate continued appropriateness.
references: AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria (revised points of focus 2022)

ragnarok.title: Critical Vulnerabilities Are Not Remediated Within Defined Timeframes
ragnarok.description: The organization does not have consistently enforced remediation SLAs and exception handling for vulnerabilities based on severity, exploitability, asset criticality, and exposure.
ragnarok.summary: Critical Vulnerabilities Are Not Remediated Within Defined Timeframes: The organization does not have consistently enforced remediation SLAs and exception handling for vulnerabilities based on severity, exploitability, asset criticality, and exposure.
ragnarok.impact: Known exploitable weaknesses may remain available to attackers beyond an acceptable risk window.
ragnarok.recommendation: Define and enforce a risk-based vulnerability remediation lifecycle.

soc2.name: Detects and monitors vulnerabilities and configuration changes
Identifies and mitigates business disruptions and risks

remediation.solution: Define and enforce a risk-based vulnerability remediation lifecycle.

Classify vulnerabilities using severity plus exploitability, exposure, business criticality, and threat intelligence
Define remediation SLAs by risk tier
Automatically assign owners and due dates
Validate fixes through rescanning
Require documented risk acceptance for SLA exceptions
Escalate overdue critical/high items
Report aging and SLA compliance to management
remediation.validation: Approved vulnerability-management standard, scan coverage report, SLA dashboard, remediation tickets, rescans, and approved exceptions.
remediation.priorityRationale: Known vulnerabilities with no controlled remediation window can create direct compromise paths.

ragnarok.summary: Production Changes Can Be Implemented Without Independent Approval: Production changes are not consistently subject to documented request, risk assessment, testing, peer review, authorization, rollback planning, and post-change verification.
ragnarok.impact: Unauthorized or defective changes may introduce security weaknesses, service outages, data corruption, or untraceable configuration drift.

soc2.name: Authorizes, designs, develops/acquires, configures, documents, tests, approves, and implements changes

evidence.summary: Change tickets sampled did not consistently demonstrate independent approval, security impact assessment, testing evidence, or rollback procedures.

remediation.solution: Implement a controlled production change process with appropriate segregation of duties.

Classify standard, normal, and emergency changes
Document risk/security impact and dependencies
Require peer review and authorization before implementation
Attach test evidence
Document rollback / recovery steps
Restrict direct production access
Log deployments and configuration changes
Perform retrospective approval and review for emergency changes
remediation.validation: Sampled production changes show request, approval, test evidence, deployment record, rollback plan, and emergency-change review where applicable.
remediation.priorityRationale: Uncontrolled changes can bypass otherwise effective security controls and directly affect system reliability.

Document retention requirements
Run scheduled restore tests for representative systems and data
Perform broader disaster-recovery exercises
Track failures and recovery-time results to closure
